sub: Named after al-kāfirūn, “the disbelievers”, addressed in ayah 1
theme: A clear, final answer to offers of compromise in worship. The Prophet ﷺ declares that his worship and theirs will never be mixed: they have their religion, and he has his.
story: Revealed in Makkah according to most, though one view says Madinah. Quraysh’s leaders had not yet given up hope of striking a deal with the Prophet ﷺ, and made offers at different times.

Reportedly al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, Umayyah ibn Khalaf and others proposed: “You worship our gods for a year, and we will worship your God for a year.” Another offer was: “Just touch some of our idols and we will believe you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said he would wait for his Lord’s command, and this surah came. He recited it to them at the Kaʿbah, and they gave up hope of any compromise.

sections.title: No compromise in worship
sections.meaning: Say to the disbelievers: I do not worship what you worship, and you do not worship what I worship. I will never worship what you worship, and you will not worship what I worship. You have your religion, and I have mine.
points: I don’t worship what you worship; you don’t worship what I worship
Nor will I ever; nor will you
You have your religion, and I have mine
sections.matters: It draws a clear line in belief and worship. Peaceful dealings with others are allowed, but a deal that mixes Allah’s worship with other worship is not. The Prophet ﷺ taught it as a bedtime recitation that frees one from shirk.
sections.story: Quraysh’s leaders offered a deal: the Prophet ﷺ would worship their gods for a year and they would worship Allah for a year, or he would just touch their idols. This surah refused every such offer for good.
explained: Qul: say it openly. The repetition is not empty. In one view, ayat 2–3 are about now and 4–5 about the future: no deal today, and none ever. In another, 2–3 deny sharing the same object of worship and 4–5 deny sharing the same way of worship.

Their worship, mixed with shirk, is not true worship of Allah, and the Prophet ﷺ worships only as Allah taught. The repetition also answers how often they repeated their offer. Lakum dīnukum wa-liya dīn: you have your religion and I have mine, and each will answer for his own deeds.
teaches: Worship belongs to Allah alone, with no bargaining.
Be clear and firm about your beliefs.
Fair dealings with others are fine; mixing religions is not.
Recite this surah before sleeping, as the Prophet ﷺ taught.
sections.hook: Ayat 3 and 5 are word-for-word the same. Ayah 2 uses a verb, lā aʿbudu, while ayah 4 uses a noun and past tense: lā ana ʿābidun mā ʿabadtum.

groups.text: The Prophet ﷺ is told to address the disbelievers openly.
I don’t worship what you worship, and you don’t worship what I worship.
I will never worship what you worship, and you will not worship what I worship.
You have your religion, and I have mine.

1.explain: Qul: say it publicly and firmly. Yā ayyuhā al-kāfirūn: addressed first to the Quraysh leaders who offered a deal, and through them to disbelief in every form.
1.why: Quraysh’s leaders offered that the Prophet ﷺ worship their gods for a year and they would worship Allah for a year, or that he touch some of their idols. He waited for his Lord’s command, and this surah came.

2.explain: Lā aʿbudu mā taʿbudūn: I do not worship the idols and false gods you worship, openly or inwardly. In one view, this is about the present.

3.explain: Nor do you worship the One I worship: Allah alone. Worship mixed with shirk is not true worship of Him.

4.explain: Nor will I ever worship what you worship. Either this looks to the future, or it rejects their way of worship, which they invented themselves.

5.explain: Nor will you worship what I worship. Repeated to show this has become their fixed state; it addresses those Allah knew would never believe.

6.explain: Lakum dīnukum wa-liya dīn: your religion is yours and mine is mine. It rejects any mixing of the two, and each will be judged by his own deeds.
